rationale: The Court is most likely to reverse on standing with a narrow TransUnion/Spokeo-based holding that Havens does not extend to a no-intent-to-book “audit,” adopting an administrable requirement of some genuine plan to use the service or comparable downstream consequence. Separate writings are most likely from the dissenters (to defend Havens-style informational injury) and from Justices Gorsuch/Thomas (to emphasize separation-of-powers and limits on regulation-created standing).
